title: C4OS Grill Question 038 - Codex Plugin Compatibility Boundary

questions.label: What minimum Codex plugin subset should C4OS support?
questions.help: Recommended: keep Codex package metadata in .codex-plugin/plugin.json, but use agents/c4os.yaml as the only C4OS app-shell contribution contract.
options: Codex package metadata plus agents/c4os.yaml for C4OS shell contributions
Only C4OS-specific plugins with no Codex plugin.json requirement
Codex skills only; no app plugin package compatibility

questions.label: Should bundled built-in plugins be uninstallable?
questions.help: Recommended: built-in plugins are always available from the app install but disabled by default unless the shell requires them. Users disable/enable, not uninstall.
options: Disable-only; bundled plugins cannot be uninstalled
Removable from Settings but restored on app update

questions.label: What icon format should plugin metadata support first?
questions.help: Recommended: Lucide icon name first, with custom asset icons deferred. This matches the shell's icon-button UI direction.
options: Lucide name plus SVG asset path

questions.label: How should C4OS handle agents/c4os.yaml version incompatibility?
questions.help: Recommended: require a schemaVersion, disable incompatible plugins, and show the reason in Settings. Migration can be a later explicit capability.
options: Require schemaVersion; disable incompatible plugins with visible reason
Best-effort load and ignore unknown fields
Reject app startup if a bundled plugin is incompatible

questions.label: Notes or corrections
questions.help: Clarify plugin root layout, app-installed versus user-installed plugins, validation rules, or what C4OS should borrow from Codex plugin.json.
